overview: Revvity (formerly PerkinElmer, renamed in 2023 after selling its Applied, Food and Enterprise Services business) is a health science company providing reagents, instruments, software and diagnostic testing that span the workflow from life sciences research discovery to clinical diagnosis. The company operates two segments, Life Sciences (reagents/BioLegend, instruments, scientific software) and Diagnostics (newborn/reproductive health screening, immunodiagnostics via EUROIMMUN), selling into pharma, biotech, academic, government and clinical laboratory customers in more than 160 countries. Headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts with roughly 11,000 employees, Revvity is a member of the S&P 500 and trades on the NYSE under RVTY.

business_model.summary: Revenue is split roughly evenly between Life Sciences (reagents, instruments and scientific software sold largely to pharma/biotech/academic researchers) and Diagnostics (newborn screening and reproductive health testing, plus immunodiagnostics reagents/instruments for hospitals and labs). A meaningful and growing share of revenue is recurring - consumable reagents, kits, software subscriptions/maintenance and testing services - while instrument and software license sales are more transactional/lumpy.
business_model.customer_type: B2B - pharmaceutical/biotech companies, CROs, academic and government research institutions, hospitals, clinical/reference labs and public health authorities
business_model.geographic_mix: Americas ~45%, Europe ~31%, Asia ~24% (nine months ended October 2026); roughly 60% of revenue generated outside the United States

competitive_position.market_position: Mid-cap specialist with leading or top-tier positions in niche categories - notably newborn/prenatal screening and antibody/flow-cytometry reagents (BioLegend) - but far smaller in overall scale than diversified life-science-tools leaders such as Thermo Fisher (~$45B revenue), Danaher (~$25B) and Agilent (~$7B) versus Revvity's ~$2.9B.

moat_factors.factor: Regulatory approvals/installed base in newborn screening
moat_factors.description: FDA/CE-marked screening platforms (NeoBase, GSP, EONIS) and decades-long relationships with state/national newborn screening programs create high switching costs and regulatory barriers to entry
35,000+ SKUs of antibodies, assay kits and cell-biology reagents used across academic and biopharma research create a sticky, high-margin consumables franchise
ChemDraw, Signals Notebook/Research and the newly acquired ACD/Labs platform are embedded in pharma R&D workflows, creating recurring SaaS-like revenue and switching costs
Extensive patent portfolio (e.g., HTRF, AlphaLISA, Pin-point base editing) and licensing relationships support differentiated assay technologies
Established global sales/service network (~2,000 reps in ~40 countries) but materially smaller scale and R&D budget than mega-cap peers limits pricing power

weaknesses: Sub-scale versus Thermo Fisher, Danaher and Agilent in R&D spend, purchasing leverage and distribution reach
Exposure to cyclical, policy-sensitive academic and government research funding (NIH budget uncertainty)
Immunodiagnostics segment losing share/revenue, including to Chinese local competitors in Asia-Pacific
High intangible assets (~$9B, including ~$6.6B goodwill) carry impairment risk if acquired businesses underperform
Growth has historically depended heavily on M&A/licensing rather than purely organic innovation

growth_drivers: Life Sciences Solutions and Software growth (BioLegend reagents, ChemDraw/Signals, newly acquired ACD/Labs) running ahead of company average (segment organic growth ~9% in Q3 2026)
Reproductive Health/newborn screening expansion (NeoLSD, EONIS, Vanadis NIPT, Revvity Omics genomic testing) as birth-related and genomic testing volumes grow
Bolt-on M&A in high-growth niches - ACD/Labs (scientific software, closed Q1 2026) and pending Human Cell Design (preclinical metabolic disease models, Toulouse, France)
AI integration across products (Phenologic.AI, Living Image Synergy AI, EUROPattern Classifier) and internal operations to drive differentiation and efficiency
Portfolio simplification - divesting the lower-growth China Immunodiagnostics business (~6% of FY2025 revenue) to sharpen focus on higher-margin, higher-growth lines
Margin expansion from restructuring/cost-containment actions (workforce reductions affecting ~7% of staff in 2026) and tariff refunds
Improving biopharma funding and M&A activity, plus greater clarity on NIH funding, supporting a gradual recovery in instrument and research spending

business.description: Revenue is highly dependent on pharma/biotech R&D budgets and government/academic research funding, which have been volatile amid NIH funding uncertainty and a cautious U.S. spending environment
Aggressive competition from larger, better-resourced players (Thermo Fisher, Danaher, Agilent) and specialized Chinese rivals pressures pricing and share, particularly in Immunodiagnostics
Rapid technological change requires continuous new product investment; failure to commercialize in time risks losing share
Growth strategy relies on acquisitions (ACD/Labs, pending Human Cell Design) and divestitures (China IDX); integration or deal failures could dilute returns

financial.description: ~$2.65B of senior unsecured notes outstanding after repaying the 2026 Notes in July 2026; cash fell to $593M from $920M, partly funding debt repayment and smaller buybacks
~60% of business conducted outside the U.S., generating meaningful foreign-exchange translation risk to reported revenue and earnings
~$9.0B of net intangible assets, including ~$6.6B goodwill, create impairment risk if segment growth or valuation assumptions deteriorate

regulatory.description: Diagnostics products are subject to extensive and evolving FDA (U.S.) and IVDR (EU) regulation; noncompliance risks recalls, fines or loss of authorizations
U.S.-China and broader tariff actions (including the 2026 Supreme Court IEEPA ruling and subsequent CBP refund process) create cost and planning uncertainty despite near-term refunds received
Sale of the China Immunodiagnostics business requires Chinese regulatory/product approvals and is not expected to close until end of fiscal 2027, creating execution and timing risk
Genomic/diagnostic data handling is subject to tightening U.S., EU and UK privacy laws

macro.description: NIH and other public research funding changes directly affect a meaningful customer base
Slower China biopharma/academic spending and local competition have weighed on results, prompting the planned China IDX divestiture
Fixed-rate note structure limits near-term rate sensitivity, but refinancing costs could rise on future issuance
Trade protectionism, geopolitical conflicts (e.g., Ukraine) and potential government funding shutdowns can disrupt customers and supply chains

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Life sciences tools and diagnostics demand is recovering gradually after a 2023-2025 destocking and funding-driven slowdown; management guided to roughly 5% organic growth for FY2026 (up from an initial 2-3% guide) as biopharma funding, M&A activity and NIH funding clarity improve, while academic/government spending remains comparatively soft
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - instrument/capex-type sales are cyclical and sensitive to biopharma and public research funding, while reagent/consumable and testing-service revenue is more stable and recurring
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low-to-moderate - mostly fixed-rate long-term debt, but higher rates raise refinancing costs and can pressure biotech customer funding/capex

recent_developments.event: Reported Q3 2026 results beating estimates: reported revenue $728.9M (+4% YoY), pro forma revenue $710M (+7% organic); adjusted EPS $1.38 (pro forma adjusted $1.37) vs. consensus ~$1.30; shares rose roughly 6% on the print
Raised full-year 2026 guidance (pro forma, excluding China IDX) to ~$2.86B revenue, ~5% organic growth, and pro forma adjusted EPS of $5.40-$5.45
CFRA upgraded RVTY from Hold to Buy; KeyBanc raised its price target to $165 (Overweight); UBS initiated coverage at Neutral with a $140 target
Signed a definitive agreement to divest the China Immunodiagnostics business (~6% of FY2025 revenue); close expected by end of fiscal 2027 pending Chinese regulatory approvals
Repaid in full the €500 million (~$571M) 1.875% Senior Unsecured Notes at maturity
Entered a definitive agreement to acquire Human Cell Design (preclinical metabolic-disease cell models, Toulouse, France) for ~€45M plus up to €8M earnout; expected to close Q4 2026
Completed acquisition of Advanced Chemistry Development Inc. (ACD/Labs), a scientific software provider, for $72M cash plus up to $8M contingent consideration, added to the Life Sciences segment

U.S. Supreme Court ruled the International Emergency Economic Powers Act does not authorize the tariffs previously imposed, leading to a CBP refund process under which Revvity applied for $20.2M of tariff refunds

Conducted restructuring/cost-containment actions affecting ~7% of the workforce through nine months of fiscal 2026, driving segment margin improvement (Diagnostics adjusted operating margin rose to 29.9% in Q3 2026 from 25.1%)
Scheduled Investor Day to update strategy and financial targets

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Prahlad Singh said end-market conditions continue to improve and that Q3 2026 results were meaningfully ahead of expectations, with Life Sciences organic growth (~9%) outpacing Diagnostics. Management is divesting the slower-growth, lower-margin China Immunodiagnostics business to sharpen portfolio focus, while continuing bolt-on M&A (ACD/Labs, Human Cell Design) in software and life-sciences tools. An Investor Day on November 13, 2026 is expected to provide further detail on medium-term targets.

bull_case: Organic growth and guidance have been raised twice in 2026 (from 2-3% to ~5%), signaling a genuine inflection in life-sciences end-market demand after a multi-year destocking/funding slowdown
Margin expansion is coming through faster than expected - Diagnostics adjusted operating margin rose nearly 500bps in Q3 2026 - driven by restructuring benefits, tariff refunds and favorable mix

Portfolio simplification (divesting slower-growth China Immunodiagnostics) plus disciplined bolt-on M&A in higher-growth software and life-sciences niches should improve the overall growth/margin profile
Leading, regulation-protected positions in newborn/reproductive health screening and a broad BioLegend reagent catalog provide durable, high-margin recurring revenue
Multiple sell-side upgrades (CFRA to Buy, KeyBanc target raised to $165) after the Q3 beat suggest improving sentiment, and an upcoming Investor Day could catalyze further re-rating
bear_case: Revvity remains sub-scale versus Thermo Fisher, Danaher and Agilent, limiting R&D firepower, purchasing leverage and ability to compete on price
A large share of revenue still depends on cyclical, policy-sensitive academic/government and biopharma capex, which could reverse if NIH funding or biopharma funding conditions worsen again

Immunodiagnostics continues to lose revenue, partly to Chinese local competitors, even as the company divests its own China Immunodiagnostics unit - leaving execution risk on both sides of that transaction through its 2027 expected close
~$9B of intangible assets (including ~$6.6B goodwill) create meaningful impairment risk if growth assumptions in acquired businesses or reporting units disappoint

Share repurchases have slowed sharply in 2026 (from $652.5M in the first nine months of 2025 to $102.6M in the same period of 2026) as cash was redirected to debt repayment, reducing a prior source of EPS support
